idea-plugin.name: NetCDF, HDF5 & NumPy Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
Open NetCDF (.nc, .nc4, .cdf), HDF5 (.h5, .hdf5, .he5) and NumPy (.npy, .npz) files in a read-only viewer inside PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, DataSpell, CLion and the other JetBrains IDEs.

Double-click a file in the Project view. You see its structure, its metadata and its values without writing a Python script or running ncdump.

NetCDF and HDF5

  • A tree of groups, variables and dimensions, with shape, type, chunks and compression for each variable.
  • Attributes and CF metadata: units, long names, scale_factor and add_offset, fill values, and time axes decoded to dates (calendars included).
  • A heatmap of any 2D slice. Pick the row and column dimensions, and move a slider for each other dimension. Eight colour maps, percentile or fixed range, log scale.
  • A line plot for 1D variables, and a time series for the point you click in the heatmap.
  • Stats for the slice on screen (min, max, mean, std, fill count), a paged value table, and CSV export of the current slice.
  • Big files open fast: only the header and the chunks a slice needs are read.

NumPy .npy and .npz

  • The array list of an .npz, with shape, dtype and size for each array.
  • Stats from all values (min, max, mean, std, NaN and Inf counts), and a value table with paging.
  • A heatmap for 2D arrays and an image view for H x W x 3 or 4 arrays.
  • Save an array or a slice as .npy or CSV.

Everything is read-only and offline. The viewer makes no network calls and never changes your file.

Free and open source (MIT). Source code and issues: github.com/theluckystrike/science-data-viewer-jetbrains.

idea-plugin.change-notes: 0.1.0: first release. NetCDF-3, NetCDF-4 and HDF5 viewer with CF decoding, heatmaps, line plots, stats and CSV export. NumPy .npy and .npz viewer with stats, value table, heatmap and image view.
